messages:
oliver: Heads up — did a quick perf sweep on tracing exports for python infer service. Seeing ~2-5ms p99 regressions when using the default blocking OTLP gRPC exporter.

maya: Details? which exporter + config, and on what infra?

oliver: python opentelemetry-sdk + OTLP gRPC (otlp_exporter). We were using sync export + relying on shutdown flush. Workers are high-throughput, mostly long-lived but some autoscale short-lived ones. Spans get dropped and latency spikes on export backpressure.

kevin: We see a similar pattern in go. Default batch exporter settings (like 5s/512 spans) are too coarse for low-latency inference. Two approaches: smaller batches + async handoff, or emit fewer spans (coarser granularity).

chen: Proposal: emit one "inference" span per request with attributes (model, model_version, seq_len, tokens_generated, route_id, fallback_used). Avoid per-token spans unless debug mode is on.

eva: +1. Also strip prompt text by default — huge attr payloads kill exporter throughput. Use attribute limits and a redact/pseudonymize policy for tenant-facing fields.

oliver: Also debating agent vs direct exporter. Local OTEL collector in same AZ reduced p99 in our tests versus direct remote OTLP gRPC. But it adds another hop and operational surface. For hosted infra, local collector seems fine. For private deployments, direct export may be needed.

maya: What about using OTLP/HTTP with a non-blocking background sender? HTTP is easier to route through proxies. But the SDK still needs an async queue; configs differ across python/go/rust.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for trace-export-tweak -> eng-runtime at 2030506800

kevin: On instrumentation: avoid making KV cache an inner span. It adds noise. Better to record kvcache_hit=true on the request span and emit a small metric counter for cache hit/miss.

chen: We should standardize resource attributes across languages: service.name, service.instance.id, deployment.environment, region, tenant.id (only when allowed). Will put a canonical list in the spec.

eva: Failure modes: exporter errors shouldn't block inference. Drop spans but increment a diagnostic counter (tracing.export.errors) and emit a single warn log per minute per instance to detect sustained failures. Avoid repeated log floods.

oliver: For serverless workers that spin up per-invocation, background batching is unreliable — those need synchronous flush-on-complete or a short blocking flush with a tight timeout. For long-lived GPU workers, use async batching with larger buffers and disk-backed queue if exporter is flaky.

maya: Can we have a tiny init-shim in each language that returns a closeable tracer provider + context manager? Patterns: env-based config (REDWOOD_TRACE_ENABLED, REDWOOD_TRACE_SAMPLING, REDWOOD_TRACE_EXPORTER), and a guaranteed flush on graceful shutdown.

kevin: Also add a flag to switch kvcache attribute -> metrics. That lets customers toggle noise without code changes.

chen: Sampling defaults: 1% in prod, 100% in canary/qa, with per-route overrides for high-impact endpoints. We should make it configurable via the shim and support dynamic overrides from control plane.

eva: Tests: need a harness that can replay synthetic inference traces, simulate exporter failures, validate attribute sizes (trimmed to 1200 bytes ideally), and measure added p50/p99. Add tests to infra repo and run in PR jobs.

oliver: Action items: maya to draft the init-shim spec + config envs; kevin to prototype kvcache attr -> metric toggle in go; chen to propose canonical resource attrs and PII rules; eva to add test harness and failure-mode tests. I'll open a tracking issue and link PRs.

maya: I'll have a doc sketch by EOD tomorrow, will ping here. cc @security for tenant.id handling and PII guidance.

oliver: Thanks all :thumbsup:
